description.value: The study examined behavioral and fMRI BOLD responses during cognitive reappraisal of three socio-emotional stimulus types in adults with generalized social anxiety disorder compared with healthy controls.

design.value: A between-group study comparing 27 unmedicated adults with generalized SAD and 27 healthy controls during three socio-emotional fMRI tasks, each containing React and Reappraise conditions; behavioral negative emotion ratings, BOLD signal magnitude, and BOLD temporal dynamics were analyzed.

description.value: This questionnaire assesses both fear and behavioral avoidance of social situations.

name.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

description.value: Two PhD-level clinical psychologists assessed each potential participant using the Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version.
Handedness was assessed with the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory.
After each trial, participants provided a negative emotion rating using a button response pad by responding to 'How negative do you feel?' (1 = not at all to 5 = very much).

source_definition.value: The tasks were composed of ‘React’ and ‘Reappraise’ conditions.

description.value: Adults who met DSM-IV-TR criteria for primary generalized SAD; the selected subgroup had the highest social anxiety symptom severity.

inclusion_criteria.value: principal diagnosis of current generalized SAD, defined as greater than moderate anxiety/fear for five or more distinct social situations

exclusion_criteria.value: current psychiatric disorders other than SAD, generalized anxiety disorder, agoraphobia without a history of panic attacks, dysthymia, or specific phobia

recruitment_method.value: clinician referrals and advertisements on community and online bulletin boards

diagnostic_instrument.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

clinical_characteristics.value: Current Axis-I co-morbidity included two with panic attacks, two with generalized anxiety disorder, two with dysthymia, and two with specific phobia. Past Axis-I co-morbidity included six with major depression, one with post-traumatic stress disorder, four with substance abuse, and one with eating disorder. The subgroup had LSAS-SR scores of 85–102.

medication_status.value: Unmedicated; minimum of three months since stopping pharmacotherapy. Seven reported past pharmacotherapy.

description.value: Healthy controls with no lifetime history of psychiatric disorders and no current or past history of DSM-IV disorders.

inclusion_criteria.value: no current or past history of DSM-IV disorders

exclusion_criteria.value: any current or past psychiatric disorders

medical_condition.value: no lifetime history of psychiatric disorders

task_description.value: Participants viewed color photos of faces displaying Ekman facial action coded anger and contempt facial expressions. Each trial included a Look or Reframe cue, a looming harsh facial stimulus, and a negative emotion rating.

instructions.value: React by engaging in the picture and thinking ‘This person is upset with me; angry with me’, or reappraise, for example by thinking ‘Maybe this person just had a bad day’.

stimuli.value: Color photos of looming harsh faces displaying anger and contempt facial expressions.

task_performance_measures.value: negative emotion rating; percent reduction in negative emotion

task_description.value: Participants watched videotaped actors delivering social criticism or praise; only the evaluation period of social criticism trials was analyzed. Participants either just watched or reframed their reaction, followed by a negative emotion rating.

instructions.value: React to social criticism by reflecting on how the statement represents something true about themselves, or reappraise by thinking ‘this is not always true’ or ‘this is only a thought, not a fact’.

stimuli.value: Videotaped actors delivering social criticism and social praise with harsh or happy evaluation-congruent facial expressions.

task_performance_measures.value: negative emotion rating; percent reduction in negative emotion

task_description.value: Participants reacted to or reframed autobiographical social anxiety-related negative self-beliefs embedded in written descriptions of participant-generated situations, followed by negative emotion ratings.

instructions.value: React by reflecting on how the negative self-belief represents something true about themselves, or reappraise by thinking of a positive coping statement that directly challenges the thoughts.

stimuli.value: Written autobiographical social anxiety situations, 16 sentences describing each situation, and participant-generated negative self-beliefs flashed in uppercase letters.

task_performance_measures.value: negative emotion rating; percent reduction in negative emotion

modality.value: functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) of blood oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) signal

instrument.value: General Electric 3-T Signa magnet with a custom-built quadrature ‘dome’ elliptical bird cage head-coil (GE Healthcare, Milwaukee, WI, USA)

description.value: Functional volumes were obtained from 22 sequential axial slices using a single-shot sequence. Functional volumes were 516 for Faces, 684 for Criticism, and 630 for Beliefs.

pulse_sequence_type.value: T2*-weighted gradient echo spiral-in/out pulse sequence

number_of_volumes.value: 516 for Faces, 684 for Criticism, and 630 for Beliefs

description.value: Three-dimensional high-resolution anatomical scans were acquired using a fast spin-echo spoiled gradient recall sequence.

Preprocessing included analysis of potential outliers, volume registration to a base image, motion correction, 4 mm isotropic Gaussian spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, linear detrending, and conversion into BOLD signal percentage change in each voxel. The first four images of each functional run were excluded; Criticism and Belief runs were concatenated before statistical analysis.

steps.value: volume registration to a base image
conversion into BOLD signal percentage change in each voxel
exclusion of the first four images of each functional run to allow for T2* equilibration effects
concatenation of the two Criticism and Belief functional runs prior to statistical analysis

hrf_model.value: Cohen’s gamma variate model of the hemodynamic response function

model_settings.value: AFNI 3dDeconvolve included baseline parameters to remove mean, linear, and quadratic trends, and motion-related variance in the BOLD signal. Regressors for the React and Reappraise conditions were convolved with the hemodynamic response function. BOLD signal intensity was computed as percentage of signal change.

estimator.value: random-effects model for second-level group statistical parametric maps

model_settings.value: Early responses were the first three time points (0–4.5 s); late responses were the last two or three time points (4.5–7.5 s or 4.5–9 s). Percent signal change for Reappraise minus React was averaged across early and late time points and compared between SAD and HC.

description.value: Participants were instructed to react normally without any attempt to control, modify, or regulate any reactions.
Participants were instructed to try and down regulate negative emotion reactions by actively reinterpreting the meaning of the emotion inducing stimulus.

definition.value: Between-group differences in the BOLD responses during Reappraise versus React for criticism; HC > SAD

multiple_comparison_method.value: AlphaSim, a Monte Carlo simulation bootstrapping program

model_representation_notes.value: Baseline parameters removed mean, linear, and quadratic trends and motion-related variance; React and Reappraise regressors were convolved with the Cohen’s gamma variate hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: Reappraisal-related activity in visual and attention-related regions was reduced in SAD compared with HC during criticism.

definition.value: Between-group differences in the BOLD responses during Reappraise versus React for faces; HC > SAD

multiple_comparison_method.value: AlphaSim, a Monte Carlo simulation bootstrapping program

model_representation_notes.value: Baseline parameters removed mean, linear, and quadratic trends and motion-related variance; React and Reappraise regressors were convolved with the Cohen’s gamma variate hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: Patients had lesser reappraisal-related BOLD responses in reappraisal-related brain regions when reappraising faces.

definition.value: Between-group differences in the BOLD responses during Reappraise versus React for beliefs; HC > SAD

multiple_comparison_method.value: AlphaSim, a Monte Carlo simulation bootstrapping program

model_representation_notes.value: Baseline parameters removed mean, linear, and quadratic trends and motion-related variance; React and Reappraise regressors were convolved with the Cohen’s gamma variate hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: Patients had lesser reappraisal-related BOLD responses in the left superior temporal gyrus when reappraising beliefs.

title.value: Criticism task: differential and common BOLD responses for Reappraise versus React

footer.value: t-value threshold ≥2.93, voxel P <0.005, minimum cluster volume threshold ≥244 mm (6 voxels × 3.438 mm), cluster P <0.01. BA = Brodmann area, xyz = Talairach and Tournoux coordinates of maximum BOLD signal intensity voxel.

description.value: Reports differential and common BOLD responses for the Criticism task.

footer.value: t-value threshold ≥2.932, voxel P <0.005, minimum cluster volume threshold ≥244 mm (6 voxels × 3.438 mm), cluster P <0.01. BA = Brodmann area, xyz = Talairach and Tournoux coordinates of maximum BOLD signal intensity voxel.

description.value: Reports differential and common BOLD responses for the Faces task.
